requirement:
The coverage overview counts documented source items carrying coverage
annotations, once per source item, and groups them by source file. Directory
summaries include these items in all descendants,
regardless of which groups are expanded. Read or parse failures that prevent
discovering annotations are visible and are not presented as a complete
absence of documentation.
rationale: I judged the three marked tests in `src/execution_coverage/book.rs` against each clause of `requirements.test-coverage.index.gaps.summary`. They cover every clause, so I found no gap. I did not request implementation source. **Counts documented items once per source item.** - `mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]` builds `code.rs`, which has a root annotation and a function `one` carrying two separate cite blocks. The test expects 2 items for that file, not 3. - The same test asserts the exact total "7 documented source items carrying coverage annotations". The total is 2 for `code.rs`, 2 for `src/direct.rs`, 1 for `src/deep/nested.rs`, 1 for `vendor/foreign.rs` and 1 for `docs_only/deep/item.rs`. - A per-annotation count would give 8 and fail this assertion. - `src/pass.rs` has no annotation and is asserted absent. **Groups by source file.** - The same test checks that each documented file has its own `data-file` row, with a per-file count cell and per-item locations such as `{file}:{line} #{selector}`. - It also checks the expected file-notes chapters. There are 5 such chapters, one per documented file. **Directory summaries include all descendants.** - The test asserts each directory summary count: `src` 3, `src/deep` 1, `vendor` 1, `docs_only` 1 and `docs_only/deep` 1. - `src` has one direct file and one nested directory, so its count includes the descendant. - `docs_only` contains only a nested directory and no direct files. Its summary count of 1 therefore comes purely from descendants. `assert_directory_contents` and the check that the ancestor has no direct `data-file` rows back this up. - The count text sits in the summary and does not depend on the `open` state of the groups. I judge the "regardless of which groups are expanded" clause satisfied by the summary count being static summary text. **Read or parse failures are visible and not shown as complete absence.** - `mod[tests]/fn[empty_documentation_and_source_failures_are_distinct]` first checks that an empty repository shows "No documented coverage gaps are present.". It then checks three failure cases: - A syntactically broken `broken.rs` shows "Source notes unavailable" and the file name, and the "No documented…" message is absent. - A corrupt `.git/index` shows "cannot discover reference sources", and again the "No documented…" message is absent. - Together these show that discovery failures are distinct from an empty result. - `mod[tests]/fn[missing_and_unreadable_sources_produce_overview_diagnostics]` covers an unreadable file (mode 000), where the overview shows "Source notes unavailable" and the file name. It covers a missing indexed file, where it shows "code.rs: current source is missing". In both cases the "No documented…" message is absent. - It also checks the boundary that missing excluded or disallowed files do not trigger a failure message. All obligations are mapped to concrete assertions, so I found no unacknowledged gap.
